title: Token usage decomposition — visualization & grooming notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick exploration of a focused console surface for breaking down API token usage into meaningful, actionable buckets so ops/product can: (1) troubleshoot noisy keys, (2) tune quotas and alerting, (3) understand route/model-level drivers of cost. This is a working doc — lots of rough ideas and questions below.

Goals / success metrics:
- Surface the dominant cost/latency drivers for a token in < 3 clicks
- Make it trivial to set or suggest quota changes from the same page
- Provide both aggregated and route-level views without overwhelming non-technical PMs/CS reps
- Reduce mean time to resolution for noisy-token incidents by 30% (tracked via incident postmortems)

Users / personas:
- Platform ops on-call: wants quick root-cause (route or model spike?) and an immediate mitigation action (soft-limit, pause key).
- CS/solutions engineer: wants shareable snapshot and recommendations to give customers.
- Product manager: needs trend/context and ability to create follow-ups (tickets, tasks).

User stories (examples):
- As an on-call engineer, I want to see which route caused a token's 5x traffic spike in the last hour so I can throttle or route-fallback it.
- As a CS rep, I want an exportable summary for a customer review call that shows cost by model and top 10 routes.

Wireframe / layout ideas (two-column variable-height):
- Header: token label, owner, tier, last seen, status pill (active | paused | restricted) + quick actions (pause key, adjust quota, open incident).
- Left column (summary):
  * Top-line KPI row: 24h tokens processed, estimated token cost, avg latency, error %
  * Trend sparkline mini charts (1h / 24h / 7d toggle) for tokens/day and cost/day
  * Anomaly badge if sudden deviation (>3x baseline) with suggested action (e.g., "Set temporary soft cap to 20 req/min")
- Right column (decomposition):
  * Stack view: contribution by model -> route -> prompt category (if tagged) for selected time range
  * Top routes list (sortable by tokens, cost, latency). Each row small inline sparkline + route breakdown button (expands inline to show sample payload distribution).
- Expandable panel: raw request timeline with ability to filter by route/model/status and to replay a request (sample sanitized payload).

Interaction details / microcopy:
- Hover on a stack segment shows absolute tokens, % of token total, median latency for that slice, and most common user agent.
- Default time window: last 24h; quick presets: 1h, 24h, 7d, last billing period
- If a token has billing attribution to a customer, show link to Billing > invoices for that customer and the last invoice snapshot.

Sample mock data (table-like text for wireframe):
Token: tok_0a9yX  | Owner: ACME Inc. | Plan: Dedicated-Prod
Time window: 2026-03-10 00:00 -> 2026-03-11 00:00
Top routes by token count:
1) /v1/generate-chat — 1,234,567 tokens — est $12.34 — median latency 180ms — errors 0.2%
2) /v1/embed — 342,110 tokens — est $3.42 — median latency 75ms — errors 0.01%
3) /v1/rerank — 89,344 tokens — est $0.89 — median latency 420ms — errors 1.4%

Backlog / actionable items (ordered):
- [P0] Route detail expand: inline sample payloads + origin header parsing (owner: Jonah). Linear: RED-234
- [P0] Soft-cap controls on token page (UI + backend throttle API) (owner: Andre). JIRA-PLAT-1421
- [P1] Automated quota suggestions: run daily heuristic to propose quantized caps (owner: Maya). linked PR above
- [P2] Export snapshot to CSV + shareable permalink (owner: Sofia)
- [P2] Add model-quantization flag to stack breakdown (to attribute quantized vs full-precision cost)

Open questions / trade-offs (notes to self):
- How to avoid exposing PII in sample payloads? Require sanitization pipeline; maybe show only headers + token counts by default.
- Should route breakdown be precomputed for fast read path? For high-volume tokens, dynamic aggregation will be slow — consider pre-aggregation with TTL.
- UX complexity: show both model and route in the stack or let users pivot? My gut: stack = model first, then route drilldown. Simpler for cost attribution.

Data signals we'd like to surface (instrumentation notes):
- normalized_token_count, model_id, route, response_time_ms, error_code_group, billing_customer_id, user_agent, region, prompt_tag (if available)
- pre-aggregates: top_n_routes_last_24h, pct_tokens_from_top_1_route, rolling_baseline_24h_mean

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Token page shows Top KPIs + Top 10 routes with tokens & estimated cost
- Can pause key and set a temporary soft-limit from the page (backend endpoint in place)
- Route rows expand to show last 5 sample sanitized payloads and header origins
- Export snapshot to CSV from the page

Accessibility & performance notes:
- Charts should degrade to accessible tables for screen readers
- Limit default returned rows to 100; lazy-load more with pagination for large token sets

Design variants to test (A/B):
A) Compact table-first layout: table of routes at top, charts below (better for ops)
B) Visual-first layout: large stack + chart, routes as secondary list (better for PM storytelling)

Meeting notes from 2026-03-03 sync with Ops:
- Ops asked for single-click "mute key" vs pause to keep ingestion but drop to lowest allowed model (idea: route-level throttling mapping)
- CS requested pre-formatted snapshot that includes recommended quota numbers and rationale text (auto-generated blurb)

Next steps (short):
- Wireframe low-fi screens (Jonah) due 2026-03-16
- Backend pre-agg feasibility spike (Andre) due 2026-03-20
- Create Linear tasks for export & soft-cap api (Maya) today

Notes / TODO (personal):
- Draft example email/text for CS when sending snapshot to customer. Keep it short: what changed, suggested action, how to undo.
- Validate cost-estimate model with billing team — current est is best-effort, need confidence interval.

Rough copy for the autogenerated recommendation card (example):
"Recommendation: top route (/v1/generate-chat) accounts for 62% of yesterday's tokens. Consider a temporary soft cap of 150 requests/min for 2 hours while you investigate. Expected cost reduction: ~40% during the cap window. Actions: [Apply soft cap] [Open ticket] [Contact support]"

End of doc — rough, iterate.
